desks.title: Retainer health and capacity — month-end review
desks.description: Ten retainers checked against the hours actually spent: where we're over-servicing, which clients have gone quiet, two renewals coming up, and whether next month needs a freelancer.
desks.brief:
## Retainer health and capacity — month-end review

**Agency** Saltbush Studio · 14 people, 9 in delivery
**Retainers** 10 clients · $88k a month
**This month** 684 hours used against 675 sold · utilisation 87% against an 80% target

### What this review is for
- Catch over-servicing before it becomes the norm
- Get ahead of two renewals and one client who has gone quiet
- Decide whether next month needs a freelancer or a hire

### Headlines
- Kelpie Pet Insurance and Copperpot Kitchens ran **39 hours over** between them — about $4.9k of unbilled time at $125 an hour
- Glasshouse Gyms used 41 of 56 hours: approvals are slow and their marketing lead has stopped coming to status calls
- Ridgeline Credit Union renews @+21d, Riverbend Water @+30d

### Capacity
1,080 billable hours available across the delivery team. Retainers took 684 and project work 256, so 940 booked.

callout.title: Kelpie: 131 hours on a 110-hour retainer
callout.body: Three rounds of changes to the quote-flow pages that weren't in scope. Rescope meeting with their head of digital @+3d: either a change request at $125 an hour, or phase 2 moves out a month.

chart.title: Hours sold vs used, by client

children.label: Move Kelpie phase 2 out a month
Scope check at every status call

blocks.p: Held with Priyanka (client services) and Owen (creative director). Every decision has an owner and a date.

ul: Kelpie: rescope meeting @+3d; no unscoped changes from today (Priyanka)
Copperpot: 18 hours over on social — community management moves to its own fee next month (Priyanka)
Glasshouse: I call their owner this week, not the account manager
Ridgeline: renewal proposal with a 6% rate rise, sent @+7d (Owen)
Riverbend: propose adding paid social at $3k a month (Priyanka)

blocks.p: Book a freelance developer for 60 hours next month rather than hiring. **Revisit the hire if development stays above 95% for a second month.**

notes.title: Status calls — what I heard
notes.body:
- Kelpie's head of digital thinks the quote-flow changes were 'fixes', not new work. They weren't — the signed brief is clear
- Copperpot loves the community replies and has no idea they're 18 extra hours
- Glasshouse's marketing lead has missed three status calls in a row
- Ridgeline wants a brand refresh next year — that's a project, not retainer work

2. Call Glasshouse's owner
3. Book the freelance dev

stickies.title: Rule
stickies.body: Anything not in the brief gets a change request — even the small ones.

images.title: Capacity board, month-end
images.prompt: Documentary photograph inside a small Australian creative agency studio at month-end: a large whiteboard wall ruled into a neat grid with thin black tape, filled with rows of blank coloured magnetic cards in yellow, coral pink and pale blue, a few rows visibly overcrowded with cards spilling past the tape line. One anonymous hand, seen from the side, moves a card from a crowded row to an emptier one. Exposed brick, a trailing pothos plant on a shelf, soft morning daylight from tall warehouse windows, shallow depth of field, natural colours, calm and organised mood. The cards and the board are completely blank, with no writing or marks.

images.title: The studio floor, late afternoon
images.prompt: Architectural interior photograph of a small independent design and marketing agency in a converted Melbourne warehouse, late afternoon. Long shared timber desks carry closed laptops, a few closed sketchbooks, mugs and a jar of pencils. Three people are seen from behind and slightly out of focus: one stands at a cork pinboard of plain colour swatches and fabric offcuts, two talk quietly at the far end of the desk. No computer screens are visible anywhere. Bare whitewashed brick walls with nothing hung on them except that pinboard, potted fiddle-leaf figs, polished concrete floor, steel-framed windows with warm low sun raking across the room and long shadows. Quiet, unhurried atmosphere, muted earthy palette, vertical composition looking down the length of the studio.

desks.title: Pitch — Bramble Ridge Outdoor rebrand and launch
desks.description: A competitive pitch for a 38-store outdoor retailer: what they told us, the story we're taking in, the scope and fee against their ceiling, and the run sheet for the room.
desks.brief:
## Pitch — Bramble Ridge Outdoor

**Prospect** 38-store outdoor gear retailer, family-owned, 30 years trading
**Ask** rebrand and a launch campaign, live in six months · **Budget** up to $240k
**Pitch** @+5d, 60 minutes, at one of their stores · **Up against** two larger agencies

### What they told us
- The brand looks like a discount store; their best customers are serious hikers
- Online is 22% of sales and growing; the stores still matter most
- Esme, the founder's daughter, now runs marketing and owns the decision

### Our angle
They don't need a new logo as much as a reason to choose them over the big-box chains — and that reason is their staff. **Lead with the people, not the gear.**

### Where it stands
Story agreed. Identity route A is in progress; its palette is on this desk. Scope prices at $247k, which is $7k over their ceiling.

callout.title: $7k over their ceiling
callout.body: Scope prices at $247k against $240k. Proposal: deliver store signage as an $8k toolkit instead of the $16k full manual, saving $8k, and land at $239k. Decide with Owen @+1d.

children.label: Staff as the voice of the brand
Gear notes tested on real trails
Launch film shot with their own staff
Two bigger agencies in the mix
Does the founder still have a veto?

ol: 0–5: Owen — why we asked to meet in a store, not a boardroom
5–15: What we heard — their words played back to them
15–30: The idea — 'Ask someone who's been there'
30–40: Identity route A, first look — Tui
50–60: Scope, timeline, fee and questions — Priyanka

blocks.p: A printed 12-page booklet and the scope at **$239k**. No deck emailed until after their decision.

ul: Timed rehearsal @+3d, with Priyanka playing Esme
Find out whether the founder will be in the room
Store-visit photos into the booklet by @+2d
Contrast-check route A: Granite type on Chalk, Chalk on Trail green

notes.title: Discovery call — what Esme told us
notes.body:
- 'We look like we sell tents to people who've never camped'
- Several of their store staff have walked the long trails; no customer knows that
- Their last agency delivered a logo and left — she wants a partner after launch
- Budget is firm at $240k; launch in six months
- Decision by @+12d

2. Identity route A review
3. Book the rehearsal room

stickies.title: Don't forget
stickies.body: Bring the store-visit photos. They're the strongest thing we have.

images.title: Store visit, the boot wall
images.prompt: Documentary photograph inside an independent, family-owned outdoor gear shop in a regional Australian town: a timber wall of plain unbranded leather hiking boots on shelves, rucksacks hanging from pegs, coiled climbing rope and a rack of rain shells in muted greens and ochres. In the middle distance a shop assistant, seen from behind, adjusts the hip belt of a rucksack on a customer whose face is turned away. Warm shop lighting mixed with daylight from the street door, worn floorboards, honest and unstaged feel, 35mm film look. Every item is plain, with no logos, tags or labels.

images.title: Identity route A, moodboard
images.prompt: Overhead flat-lay of a brand identity moodboard on a sheet of rough chalk-white watercolour paper: plain unprinted colour swatch cards in deep forest green, warm ochre and granite grey, a square of waxed canvas, a coil of worn boot lace, a pressed eucalyptus leaf, a small brass carabiner, a graphite pencil, and a torn scrap of paper printed with an abstract topographic contour-line pattern that has no labels or numbers. Soft diffused daylight from one side, gentle natural shadows, editorial still-life styling, calm earthy palette, generous space between objects.
